candidate_sources.README.md:
# Workspace drafts with asynchronous acknowledgements

open/edit/close are synchronous. The editor currently submits every edit.
A visit's latest pending text must be submitted exactly once before close or
navigation returns; submission must not wait for network acknowledgement.
Accepted writes belong to the document, survive navigation, and all settle.
Store read exposes the latest accepted draft for immediate reopen; readPersisted
exposes acknowledged data, protected by write revision against late old writes.
The provided transport accepts a write synchronously and returns a Promise.
Its start callback may synchronously open another document, reopen the same
one, hide the editor, or edit that new visit. Acceptance occurs before that hook.
Navigation priority follows call start order: a newer open/close supersedes an
outer navigation that resumes after a save-start callback. Obsolete destinations
must not render. A newly accepted edit must not be erased by old flush cleanup.

A save-status notification may appear only for the current visit's latest edit.
A pending newer edit invalidates an older acknowledgement even before its own
write is submitted. store.write(id,text,owner) round-trips an opaque owner token;
attachSaveStatus supports an owner predicate. Reopening the same document does
not give its new visit ownership of the old visit's acknowledgement.
Do not cancel accepted saves to suppress UI messages. No network failures or
retry policy are included in this fixture; each transport Promise settles once.

The search preview is transient: 40 ms quiet interval, discard pending query
on hide, reusable afterward. It is outside the editor maintenance request.

checkpoints: Several edits less than 120 ms apart produce no early write and one write containing the latest text after 120 ms of quiet.
A later editing burst saves again; empty text remains valid; editing without an open document remains a no-op.
Close, navigation, same-document reopen, and workspace disposal submit the departing visit's pending text exactly once before returning, without waiting for acknowledgement.
Reopening immediately reads accepted text even while its acknowledgement is pending.
Transport start callbacks that open, reopen, close, or edit a successor visit preserve the newest navigation and its pending edits.
Acknowledgements produce status only for the active visit's latest edit, including when a newer edit is still pending submission.
Out-of-order acknowledgements all settle without rolling persisted text back.
Search preview retains its existing delay, cancellation on hide, and subsequent reuse.
forbidden_effects: Do not discard a departing visit's pending text or submit the same consumed batch twice.
Do not let an older navigation continuation render an obsolete destination or clear a newer visit's document output.
Do not erase callback-enqueued work during cleanup of an older batch.
Do not display acknowledgement status for a retired visit or an edit superseded by a pending newer edit.
Do not cancel accepted writes to suppress status output.
Do not change search-preview behavior or introduce submission receipts, projection archives, or other APIs absent from these public sources.
lifecycle_identity: Each opening creates a distinct visit, including reopening the same document ID.
Each accepted editor edit establishes the latest opaque owner token immediately; status eligibility depends on both the exact active visit and that token.
Pending save arguments belong to the accepting document and edit, rather than whichever document is selected when the timer fires.
Accepted store writes outlive editor visits and settle independently.

obligations.text: Use the existing trailing-task utility to coalesce editor edits with a 120 ms quiet interval, submitting only the latest text in each burst and supporting subsequent bursts.

Preserve synchronous public interfaces and submit each departing visit's latest pending text exactly once before close or navigation returns, including closure through dispose; do not wait for network acknowledgement.
Preserve navigation priority by call start order across synchronous transport callbacks. A newer open or close supersedes an older request, and obsolete destinations must not render.
Preserve independent accepted writes, immediate accepted-draft reads, revision-protected persisted reads, and settlement of every accepted write.
Invalidate older status ownership as soon as a newer edit is accepted by the editor, before its delayed submission. Publish status only for the exact current visit's latest edit.
Preserve existing renderer payloads, subscription cleanup, no-selection edit behavior, and the separate search-preview timing and cancellation policy.

ordering_barriers: Record the newest edit's owner before scheduling its delayed write, so older acknowledgements are already ineligible during the quiet interval.
Consume and clear a pending batch before calling store.write; its transport callback may synchronously navigate or enqueue independent work.
Revoke the departing visit's ownership and detach its captured subscription before submitting its pending save.
Submit departing pending text before reading a replacement document, preserving immediate restoration from accepted drafts.
After callback-capable departure submission, revalidate the initiating navigation before installing or rendering its destination.
Complete departure clearing before callback-capable saving, or guard any later clearing against newer navigation.
Preserve store acceptance before invoking transport, and revision validation before updating acknowledged data.
preservation: Workspace open, edit, close, and dispose remain synchronous with their existing interfaces.
Document rendering remains {id, text} on retained open and null on retained close.
Editing without a current visit remains a no-op, and empty text is not treated as missing work.
Store events retain id, text, revision, and opaque owner; writes retain Promise completion and independent acknowledgement semantics.
Status subscriptions retain document filtering and owner-predicate filtering, with cleanup tied to the captured visit.
The trailing-task utility remains reusable and retains its distinct flush and cancel semantics.
Search preview retains its 40 ms quiet interval and discards pending queries on hide.
